pr_title: Move Vulkan includes to a central `godot_vulkan.h` header

pr_comments: What is the best way for 4.3 users to use this as of today?  scons fails to build on my Mac at the moment due to this error. 4.3 doesnt have an updated release, and 4.4 is not yet out.

Ive just done a git pull for 4.3, with an up to date 4.3 checkout to my local up to date Mac, I am still encountering this problem.  Perhaps I am missing something basic, but it looks to me like its not possible to build with scons on Mac any more?

Are there plants to allow scons to be used on Mac with 4.3? It seems, as it stands, it's not possible to use scons on Mac with stable godot.   Does anyone have a workaround for building on Mac for godot 4.3?
I have manually applied this patch to my checkout of the 4.3 branch and I can confirm for people on 4.3, that this patch does allow building on MacOS 15.1 using Xcode 16.1.

issue_context.title: Build problem with recent Clang releases
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible with Godot master (4.4 - 83d54ab2ad476ae265b323c2b88f4623b922f4c6)



### System information

MacOS 14.6.1 - Xcode Version 16.0 (16A242 - Release Candidate)

### Issue description

It seems that a stricter Clang is triggering a problem in Godot.

The issue seems to be that Objective-C++ code includes vulkan.h, which uses an `extern 'C'` block and then includes the C `stdint.h`, but for some reason recent Clang++ map '#include stdint.h' into importing the C++ module 'std_stdint_h', which is not allowed to be done from C.

The build error is like this:

```
In file included from platform/ios/keyboard_input_view.mm:33:
In file included from platform/ios/display_server_ios.h:42:
In file included from platform/ios/rendering_context_driver_vulkan_ios.h:36:
In file included from ./drivers/vulkan/rendering_context_driver_vulkan.h:46:
In file included from thirdparty/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan.h:11:
In file included from thirdparty/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_core.h:8325:
In file included from thirdparty/vulkan/include/vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_h264std.h:24:
thirdparty/vulkan/include/vk_video/vulkan_video_codecs_common.h:25:5: error: import of C++ module 'std_stdint_h' appears within extern "C" language linkage specification [-Wmodule-import-in-extern-c,15]
   25 |      #include <stdint.h>
      |      ^
thirdparty/vulkan/include/vk_video/vulkan_video_codecs_common.h:17:1: note: extern "C" language linkage specification begins here [2]
   17 |  extern "C" {
      |  ^

```

I am using this workaround, which seems a bit like brute force, hence why this is not a PR:

```
diff --git a/platform/ios/SCsub b/platform/ios/SCsub
index cf565db049..1ee114e59e 100644
--- a/platform/ios/SCsub
+++ b/platform/ios/SCsub
@@ -95,6 +95,8 @@ else:
 # (iOS) Enable module support
 env_ios.Append(CCFLAGS=["-fmodules", "-fcxx-modules"])
 
+env_ios.Append(CCFLAGS=["-Wno-module-import-in-extern-c"])
+
 
 def combine_libs(target=None, source=None, env=None):
     lib_path = target[0].srcnode().abspath
```

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce this issue you need a recent clang, like the one that was just released for Xcode 16.0.

Build Godot on MacOS, like this:

```
scons p=ios
```



### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

None is needed, just upgrading Xcode 16.0
comments:
FYI we have a fix for this issue, just need to replace the usual vulkan inclusion block with this:

```cpp
#ifdef USE_VOLK
#include <volk.h>
#else
#include <stdint.h>
#define VK_NO_STDINT_H
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>
#endif
```

If this is acceptable, then we can provide a PR.

> FYI we have a fix for this issue, just need to replace the usual vulkan inclusion block with this:
> 
> ```c++
> #ifdef USE_VOLK
> #include <volk.h>
> #else
> #include <stdint.h>
> #define VK_NO_STDINT_H
> #include <vulkan/vulkan.h>
> #endif
> ```
> 
> If this is acceptable, then we can provide a PR.

This seems like a workaround. I think the issue should be fixed in the Vulkan headers if they're doing something illegal - or in Clang if it's misled.

How should one import the C `stdint.h` in C code used from Obj-C++ with that Clang version? That's something that should be reproducible in a minimal example and can be discussed upstream with LLVM. It would seem weird to me that the solution is to stop using `stdint.h` in C code.

If does this kind of import is now indeed illegal from Obj-C++, then I guess the proposed approach is correct. It just seems convoluted, but I guess that's why Vulkan headers provide `VK_NO_STDINT_H`.

This is not a limitation with Objective-C++, it happens with plain C++ with newer clang.

Simple repro:

demo.cpp:
```
extern "C" {
#include <stdint.h>
}
```

Compile with:

```
$ c++ -c -fcxx-modules -fmodules demo.cpp
a.cpp:2:1: error: import of C++ module 'std_stdint_h' appears within extern "C" language linkage specification [-Wmodule-import-in-extern-c]
    2 | #include <stdint.h>
      | ^
a.cpp:1:1: note: extern "C" language linkage specification begins here
    1 | extern "C" {
      | ^
1 error generated.
```

The combination that triggers this is `-fcxx-modules` and `-fmodules`.

I found the documentation here:

https://clang.llvm.org/docs/Modules.html

Thanks, I can reproduce it on Fedora 40 too with Clang 18.1.6 and the above demo, with just `clang++ -fmodules demo.cpp`:
```
demo.cpp:2:1: error: import of C++ module '_Builtin_stdint' appears within extern "C" language linkage specification [-Wmodule-import-in-extern-c]
    2 | #include <stdint.h>
      | ^
demo.cpp:1:1: note: extern "C" language linkage specification begins here
    1 | extern "C" {
      | ^
1 error generated.
```
I just updated xcode on my mac and am also now encountering this issue.  Do we have a fix or recommended workaround while this is being looked into?
I have manually applied this patch to my checkout of the 4.3 branch and I can confirm for people on 4.3, that this patch does allow building on MacOS 15.1 using Xcode 16.1.

review_comments: Changes in third party files should be marked by `/* GODOT start */`, `/* GODOT end */` comments and/or have patches included (usually in the `patches` subfolder), and mentioned in the `thirdparty/README.md` (this includes seems to be part of existing patches, which should be updated).

We're unintentionally adding a stray line here, would be good to remove it (also in the .patch) to keep our changes minimal.

What's the rationale from moving the include outside the `extern "C"` scope though? Does it only work for C++ code?
The original error from Clang was that it was no longer allowed to include stdint.h in an extern "C" {} block. That is why the include was moved.
Pushed the update with the removal of the extra line.
